Eternality of God
ee-tur-NAL-i-tee of GOD
noun phrase (theology proper / divine attributes)
The divine attribute by which God is without beginning or end, transcending time, existing in the fullness of His being in an eternal present. Grounded in the divine names and self-descriptions (Psalm 90:2, from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God; Exodus 3:14, I AM THAT I AM; Revelation 1:8, which is, and which was, and which is to come).

📖 Biblical Definition

The divine attribute by which God is without beginning or end, transcending time, existing in the fullness of His being in an eternal present. God's eternality means more than mere endless duration (existing through infinite time); it means that God transcends time itself, existing in the fullness of His being independent of and above the temporal succession of moments. The biblical foundation: (1) Psalm 90:2, Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God; (2) Exodus 3:14, the divine name I AM THAT I AM (the untensed, pure being of God); (3) Revelation 1:8, I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty; (4) Psalm 102:27, thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end; (5) 2 Peter 3:8, one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day; (6) 1 Timothy 1:17, the King eternal; (7) Isaiah 57:15, the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity. The Reformed-confessional doctrine (Westminster Confession II.1, God is eternal; the Reformed-scholastic doctrine of divine eternity) holds that God is eternal in the fullness of His being, without beginning, end, or succession of moments. The substantive theological implications: God's eternality grounds His immutability (the eternal God does not change), His faithfulness (the eternal God's promises endure), and the believer's security (the eternal God is an everlasting refuge, Deuteronomy 33:27, the eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine of divine eternality against the process-theology denial (which makes God temporal and developing) and the rationalist reduction (which treats eternity as mere endless time); God transcends time, inhabits eternity, and is the unchanging, everlasting, faithful refuge of His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The divine attribute by which God is without beginning or end, transcending time, existing in the fullness of His being; Psalm 90:2 (from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God); Exodus 3:14 (I AM THAT I AM); Revelation 1:8; grounds His immutability, faithfulness, and the believer's everlasting security.

ETERNALITY OF GOD, n. phr. (theology proper / divine attributes) God is without beginning or end, transcending time, existing in the fullness of His being in an eternal present — more than endless duration; God transcends time itself. Foundation: Psalm 90:2 (from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God); Exodus 3:14 (I AM THAT I AM); Revelation 1:8 (which is, and which was, and which is to come); Psalm 102:27; 2 Peter 3:8; Isaiah 57:15 (the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity). Westminster II.1 (God is eternal). Grounds His immutability, faithfulness, and the believer's everlasting security (Deuteronomy 33:27, the eternal God is thy refuge). Held against process-theology (temporal, developing God) and the rationalist reduction (eternity as mere endless time).

📖 Key Scripture

Psalm 90:2 — "Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God."

Revelation 1:8 — "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty."

Isaiah 57:15 — "For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit."

Deuteronomy 33:27 — "The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The eternality of God is held against process theology (which makes God temporal and developing) and the rationalist reduction (which treats eternity as mere endless time); God transcends time and inhabits eternity.

expand to see more

The eternality of God is held against two opposing errors. Process theology (and open theism in some forms) makes God temporal and developing, subject to the succession of moments, learning and changing as history unfolds; this contradicts the biblical doctrine of God who inhabits eternity (Isaiah 57:15) and is the same from everlasting to everlasting (Psalm 90:2). The rationalist reduction treats divine eternity as mere endless time (God as a being who has existed for infinite time and will continue forever), missing the deeper truth that God transcends time itself, existing in the fullness of His being above the temporal succession. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive Reformed-confessional doctrine: God is eternal, without beginning, end, or succession; He transcends time and inhabits eternity; His eternality grounds His immutability (the eternal God does not change), His faithfulness (the eternal God's promises endure across all generations), and the believer's everlasting security (the eternal God is the refuge underneath whom are the everlasting arms, Deuteronomy 33:27). The eternality of God is not a cold abstraction but a substantive comfort: the believer's God is the everlasting God, the same yesterday, today, and forever, whose eternal purposes cannot fail and whose eternal arms cannot weaken.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Psalm 90:2; Exodus 3:14; Revelation 1:8; Isaiah 57:15; Westminster II.1; God without beginning, end, or succession, transcending time; grounds immutability, faithfulness, security.
